context_refs.label: Context Refs
context_refs.description: Pointers to related entries. Bare timestamp = same spine. 'spine-name::timestamp' = cross-spine. Example value: ["2026-11-02T00:00:05.000000+00:00", "other-spine::2026-11-01T12:00:00.000000+00:00"]

context_summary.label: Context Summary
context_summary.description: Prewritten narrative explaining what the context_refs contribute to understanding this entry — so an agent doesn't have to synthesize them cold. Example: "See decision-log entry for why this approach was chosen and the review entry for its known limitations."

data.context_summary: The schema edit window ( and indeed any text edit box may need this) needs line numbers. So when an error hits I know which line to move to since errors show line numbers.
The schema edit window should highlight the error or let the user click on the error and then it highlights that particular error in the schema they typed so they can fix it.

closing a step does not remove that steps count from the set of steps. We need to handle how steps collapse. Closing a single step should collapse the chain by a single link. This would mean all previous responses can remain and all responses after the removed link are cleared until the chain re-runs.

the schema editor 'Entry Form' should allow the user to tab between fields which does work BUT the context refs box hams this up and you get stuck tabbing around inside the context refs...figure it out.
